A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfiFPO work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across 11 benchmarks, baseline comparisons, ablations, and code-generation and mathematical-reasoning case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds original experiments involving UltraFeedback, alternative pivot and reward models, sequence alignment, and training-data volume in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The proposed objectives, length normalization, probability clipping, max-margin fusion, and IPO/WRPO adaptations are retained. Appendix E.2 supplies implementation details and explanatory examples without establishing a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix E.1.1 adds UltraFeedback, approximately 60k preference pairs, as an alternative training corpus to the constructed preference data. The original training sources and 11 evaluation benchmarks remain; no additional evaluation task or domain is established.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains its comparator roster. New Table 10 adds FuseChat and InfiFusion variants with sequence alignment removed as explicit comparators in the alignment ablation. Other supplementary experiments reuse existing baseline families.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces substantial additional experimental settings: Qwen2.5 pivot models from 1.5B to 14B, alternative source-model combinations, two alternative reward models, alignment-removal controls, and preference-training volumes from 25k to 100k. The original main experiments' training settings and evaluation prompts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Tables 7–12 examine dependence on training-data source, pivot architecture and size, reward model, sequence alignment, and data volume. These substantially extend validation beyond v1's component, fusion-strategy, and source-count analyses. The original ablations and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The supplementary results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 7–12 add substantial results under new settings. Examples include InfiFPO versus SFT-WRPO averages of 82.19 versus 81.58 with UltraFeedback and 84.01 versus 83.46 with the Qwen2.5-14B pivot. Additional results cover reward models, alignment removal, data scaling, and smaller pivots. Original main-table and case-study results remain unchanged; these are additional evaluations, not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–26, Appendix A's derivations, and the mathematical formulations of alternative objectives and fusion strategies are retained. The new probability-clipping example illustrates existing rules without adding a formal definition, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: sequence-level implicit fusion, the three supporting strategies, and superiority across 11 benchmarks. The headline Phi-4 average remains 79.95 to 83.33.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds interpretations concerning data construction, reward quality, alignment dependence, and applicability across pivot models. It also explains memory efficiency and interprets max-margin selection as choosing the 'smartest' source, relating this to FuseLLM's MinCE strategy. The existing limitations paragraph is relocated without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2.1 newly discloses precomputation of pivot/source log probabilities using vLLM, approximately eight GPU hours for five source models, and sequence-level storage. Supplementary experiments identify additional configurations and reward-model checkpoints. A front-page InfiXAI project address is added while the original Reallm-Labs address remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to InfiGFusion, a model-fusion review, PAD, model-merging scaling laws, and UltraFeedback. It adds a short PAD discussion and relates source selection to FuseLLM's MinCE strategy. The central positioning relative to WRPO and token-level fusion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. The limitations paragraph moves after the conclusion, existing appendices are renumbered, and a structured supplementary-experiments appendix is inserted. Author order, affiliations, project information, and the conference header are updated without extensive rewriting of the original narrative.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the tabular presentation with six experimental tables and two illustrative probability tables, numbered 7–14. The original case-study tables become Tables 15–16, and appendix material is reflowed. Figures 1–2 and the original main-table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix E substantially addresses v1's reliance on one pivot model and one constructed preference corpus by adding alternative data, multiple pivot sizes, and sensitivity and scaling tests. Precomputation details also make the efficiency claims more assessable. The claimed advantage of constructed data is confounded by changed source-model selection, and alignment removal lacks procedural detail, limiting those conclusions. Nevertheless, the broader empirical validation and practical documentation provide a substantial overall improvement.
